programme.title: Climate Impact Asia - S01:E01 - Sea Level Rise
programme.desc: By 2100 over 1 billion people on Earth will live in low-lying coastal zones. 70% of these will live in Southeast Asia, one of the most vulnerable regions in the world to climate change. The next decade will be the most critical for the future existence of these societies.

programme.title: Climate Impact Asia - S01:E02 - Tsunami Costal Lab
programme.desc: Natural hazards remain a constant challenge for over 400 million people who live in low lying communities built along major mega delta regions in coastal zones. Events like typhoons and tsunamis threaten their very survival.

programme.title: Climate Impact Asia - S01:E03 - Volcanic Field Lab
programme.desc: Many people now know that climate change is real, that they see the data or they see the observations for themselves. What's needed now is a sense of urgency. We have within the next decade exceedingly important decisions to make.

programme.title: Climate Impact Asia - S01:E04 - Food Security
programme.desc: Rice, it's a staple food for many in Asia. It provides 1/3 of the energy in the average Asian diet and is the income source for more than 500 million people. So, what is the future of our staple foods like rice? And how do we address the uncertainty that we face in these changing times?

programme.title: Breakthrough - S01:E58 - The West Is Burning
programme.desc: How did the western United States become a hotspot for unwieldy and devastating forest fires? Learn how the history of forest management and loss of public trust, coupled with climate change, have led to the conditions driving mega-fire nearly year-round.

programme.title: The Secret Lives of Sharks - S01:E02 - Hammerhead Shark
programme.desc: Travel to the Bahamas as Andy Casagrande attempts to place a fin camera on the elusive hammerhead shark… what could possibly go wrong?

programme.title: The Secret Lives of Sharks - S01:E03 - Tiger Shark
programme.desc: Ever wondered how a tiger shark hunts and feeds on its prey? Wildlife filmmaker Andy Casagrande travels off the coast of North Carolina to document never before seen behavior of one of the most misunderstood sharks in the world.

programme.title: Breakthrough - S01:E51 - Return of the Wolves

programme.title: Breakthrough - S01:E00 - Reefs Of Hope Extended Version

programme.title: Wild Ones - S01:E08 - Masters of the Sky
programme.desc: So many words describe the many ways that birds fly – pelicans and kestrels soar but owls fly silently. Parrots flock, vultures swarm and eagles swoop. Radar-accurate eyes scan the ground and slotted feathers adjust flight paths as hawks attack. But, which is the true master of the sky?

programme.title: Wild Ones - S01:E09 - Disguised

programme.title: Wild Ones - S01:E10 - Micro Predators
programme.desc: They may be small but don’t be fooled - micro predators can be deadly. From the impressive serial killer Portia spider to the hundreds of species of ants and the archerfish with its precision firing of water droplets to secure its prey Wild Ones peers through the microscope to uncover their true lethality.

programme.title: Wild Ones - S01:E11 - Most Poisonous_

programme.title: Wild Ones - S01:E12 - Migration

programme.title: Wild Ones - S01:E10 - Micro Predators
programme.desc: They may be small but don’t be fooled - micro predators can be deadly. From the impressive serial killer Portia spider to the hundreds of species of ants and the archerfish with its precision firing of water droplets to secure its prey Wild Ones peers through the microscope to uncover their true lethality.

programme.title: Wild Ones - S01:E11 - Most Poisonous_
programme.desc: You wouldn’t want to be bitten by any of these but which one has the deadliest poison? The venom from the most poisonous snake on the planet? A rare poisonous lizard? Or is it the blue ringed octopus?

programme.title: Wild Ones - S01:E12 - Migration
programme.desc: Animals, big and not so big, traverse hundreds of miles – some in search of food, others to find ideal breeding grounds. From Zebras crossing the savannahs of Africa to the huge journeys undertaken by turtles to find the perfect beach to lay their eggs – the annual and often dangerous journeys are simply mind boggling.

programme.title: Breakthrough - S01:E83 - The Great Seaweed Invasion
programme.desc: A giant mass of floating seaweed is invading popular beaches in the US and Caribbean!

programme.title: Climate Impact Asia - S01:E01 - Sea Level Rise
programme.desc: By 2100 over 1 billion people on Earth will live in low-lying coastal zones. 70% of these will live in Southeast Asia, one of the most vulnerable regions in the world to climate change. The next decade will be the most critical for the future existence of these societies.

programme.title: Climate Impact Asia - S01:E02 - Tsunami Costal Lab
programme.desc: Natural hazards remain a constant challenge for over 400 million people who live in low lying communities built along major mega delta regions in coastal zones. Events like typhoons and tsunamis threaten their very survival.

programme.title: Climate Impact Asia - S01:E03 - Volcanic Field Lab
programme.desc: Many people now know that climate change is real, that they see the data or they see the observations for themselves. What's needed now is a sense of urgency. We have within the next decade exceedingly important decisions to make.

programme.title: Climate Impact Asia - S01:E04 - Food Security
programme.desc: Rice, it's a staple food for many in Asia. It provides 1/3 of the energy in the average Asian diet and is the income source for more than 500 million people. So, what is the future of our staple foods like rice? And how do we address the uncertainty that we face in these changing times?

programme.title: Breakthrough - S01:E58 - The West Is Burning
programme.desc: How did the western United States become a hotspot for unwieldy and devastating forest fires? Learn how the history of forest management and loss of public trust, coupled with climate change, have led to the conditions driving mega-fire nearly year-round.

programme.title: The Secret Lives of Sharks - S01:E02 - Hammerhead Shark
programme.desc: Travel to the Bahamas as Andy Casagrande attempts to place a fin camera on the elusive hammerhead shark… what could possibly go wrong?

programme.title: The Secret Lives of Sharks - S01:E03 - Tiger Shark
programme.desc: Ever wondered how a tiger shark hunts and feeds on its prey? Wildlife filmmaker Andy Casagrande travels off the coast of North Carolina to document never before seen behavior of one of the most misunderstood sharks in the world.

programme.title: Breakthrough - S01:E51 - Return of the Wolves
programme.desc: Capture teams from the U.S. National Park Service track down and relocate wolves to Isle Royale National Park in Lake Superior under an ambitious initiative to restore balance to a wilderness ecosystem.

programme.title: Breakthrough - S01:E00 - Reefs Of Hope Extended Version
programme.desc: With new state-of-the-art tools and technologies that include curious underwater vehicles and hydrodynamic modeling, scientists have hope of better understanding the threats to coral communities while finding the source to restock reefs worldwide.

programme.title: Wild Ones - S01:E08 - Masters of the Sky
programme.desc: So many words describe the many ways that birds fly – pelicans and kestrels soar but owls fly silently. Parrots flock, vultures swarm and eagles swoop. Radar-accurate eyes scan the ground and slotted feathers adjust flight paths as hawks attack. But, which is the true master of the sky?

programme.title: China's Green Revolution Ep.2
programme.desc: China's ecological civilization and achievements are celebrated through stories of green development, like the Saihanba and Kubuqi restoration projects.

programme.title: Grand Song of the Dong - Natural Oriental Harmony
programme.desc: The Grand Song of the Dong is a polyphonic folk singing tradition of the Dong ethnic group. Performers from several villages gather together to sing, unaccompanied. The songs, which describe the history, beliefs, customs, and emotions of the Dong people, are an important part of their cultural identity and contribute significantly to their social cohesion. Generally sung in the Dong language, which has no written form, they are passed on orally from one generation to the next. Classified into various genres - including narrative and love songs, drinking and funeral songs - they are often accompanied by clapping, stomping, and dancing. Sung on occasions such as festivals, weddings, and funerals, the Grand Song, as a valuable part of the Dong ethnic group's cultural heritage, reflects their wisdom and creativity, as well as their harmony with nature.

programme.title: China Untapped: Huzhou
programme.desc: Located in the east of China, on the south shore of Taihu Lake, Huzhou has been well-known for its richness in resources and blooming in silk trade since the ancient times. Guided by the concept of "lucid waters and lush mountains are invaluable assets", Huzhou now is committed to developing green industries. In this episode, CGTN hosts Tianran He and Hannah Wilson travelled to Huzhou, where they tried a variety of guesthouse hotels in the Moganshan Mountains; experienced the life of digital nomads in Anji's countryside; learned about the eco-concepts behind China's traditional architectures in Nanxun Ancient Town; and explored the development of eco-agriculture powered by high-tech along the Taihu Lake. All these phenomena demonstrate that economic development and environmental protection can achieve harmonious coexistence, and that civilization thrives if ecology is prosperous.

programme.title: National Treasure Under Fire Ep.3
programme.desc: Ancient texts were saved through relocation efforts during the War of Resistance against Japanese Aggression. Behind each rescue was a determination to preserve China's cultural heritage. These precious texts now carry the stories our forefathers, how they fought to safeguard history and the civilization these works represent.

programme.title: From Stone to Story
programme.desc: China's profound stone carving culture dates back to the Han Dynasty (202 BC - 220 AD) and flourished during the Tang Dynasty (618 - 907 AD), evolving into a distinctive art form and unique cultural practice. Among many places famous for stone carving, Hui'an County - through generations of dedicated artisans - has risen to prominence and earned the esteemed title of "World Capital of Stone Carving," awarded by the World Crafts Council. The county's skilled stonemasons are celebrated for their ability to transform ordinary pieces of rock into beautiful works of art. This episode shines a spotlight on the intangible cultural heritage of Hui'an stone carving and reveals how it has been influenced by the area's close proximity to the sea.

programme.title: From Stone to Story
programme.desc: China's profound stone carving culture dates back to the Han Dynasty (202 BC - 220 AD) and flourished during the Tang Dynasty (618 - 907 AD), evolving into a distinctive art form and unique cultural practice. Among many places famous for stone carving, Hui'an County - through generations of dedicated artisans - has risen to prominence and earned the esteemed title of "World Capital of Stone Carving," awarded by the World Crafts Council. The county's skilled stonemasons are celebrated for their ability to transform ordinary pieces of rock into beautiful works of art. This episode shines a spotlight on the intangible cultural heritage of Hui'an stone carving and reveals how it has been influenced by the area's close proximity to the sea.

programme.title: National Treasure Under Fire Ep.5
programme.desc: Ancient texts were saved through relocation efforts during the War of Resistance against Japanese Aggression. Behind each rescue was a determination to preserve China's cultural heritage. These precious texts now carry the stories our forefathers, how they fought to safeguard history and the civilization these works represent.

programme.title: Wild Stars of the Forest
programme.desc: Orangutans, leopards, chimpanzees, sloth bears, tigers and more! Year-round monitoring captures hunting and social interactions up close, revealing unique survival skills in China's rainforests.

programme.title: Suzhou Fans
programme.desc: Suzhou, known as the "Venice of China," is also famous for its traditional crafts. And one of the most elegant and exquisite crafts is Suzhou fans. Celebrated for their exquisite design and fine quality, they’re popularly associated with literati. How come Suzhou gave birth to such a variety of fans? How can we appreciate their beauty in the modern world? In this episode, we are discovering more stories behind Suzhou fans.

programme.title: China Bound: Xiamen
programme.desc: What's it like in one of China's happiest cities? Tianran is in sunny Xiamen on China's southeast coast, visiting the city's famous "island of music" and sampling local delicacies like shark meatballs, shacha noodles and fish in "soy sauce water". He'll discover former fishing villages turned hipster havens, drink tea with locals beneath traditional tenement buildings, and visit a student enclave brimming with creative startup energy.

programme.title: Living Arts of Huizhou
programme.desc: This is Huangshan in eastern China. In this city, you’ll encounter one of China’s most traditional building styles: Hui-style architecture. How does Hui style set this region apart? What’s life like for people living in these houses? With these questions in mind, we’re embarking on a journey to decode Hui-style architecture.

programme.title: China Bound: Chengdu
programme.desc: Tianran spends 3 days in Chengdu, the capital of Sichuan Province and UNESCO's first City of Gastronomy. He dives deep into Chengdu culture, exploring the infamous "mala" numbing and spicy flavors of Sichuanese street food and hotpot, and visiting historical attractions like Wuhou Shrine, Du Fu's Thatched Cottage, and the Jinsha Site Museum, which houses exquisite relics from a 3,000-year-old kingdom uncovered beneath the streets of Chengdu. Of course, no visit to this city is complete without seeing giant pandas and enjoying a cup of tea while getting your ears cleaned in the iconic People's Park. After all, when in Chengdu, do as the locals do.

programme.title: Exploring the "National Quintessence" - Peking Opera
programme.desc: In this episode, we invite viewers to delve into Peking Opera, celebrated as the "Oriental Opera." The program visits Hu Wenge, the third-generation inheritor of the Mei School; Fu Boyang, grand disciple of Meng Guanglu and dean of Jixiang Grand Theatre; and Guo Xiaojing, a top Douyin influencer specializing in Peking Opera. Join host Yegor as we explore Peking Opera's history, immerse in its traditional artistic atmosphere, witness behind-the-scenes preparations and makeup processes, and discover the passion of today's youth for this art form. We'll also visit the Beijing Guoyi Children's Peking Opera Troupe to see how Peking Opera shapes the lives of young students.

programme.title: China Untapped: Changsha
programme.desc: The city of Changsha is one of central China's powerhouses. It's a leader in both the construction machinery industry and in media - Changsha was China's first UNESCO "Creative City". It's also one of China's best-known cities for its nightlife. The soul of a city is in its people, and this episode focuses on the women of Changsha who are helping to innovate, change and further develop this city they call home.

programme.title: Exploring the "National Quintessence" - Peking Opera
programme.desc: In this episode, we invite viewers to delve into Peking Opera, celebrated as the "Oriental Opera." The program visits Hu Wenge, the third-generation inheritor of the Mei School; Fu Boyang, grand disciple of Meng Guanglu and dean of Jixiang Grand Theatre; and Guo Xiaojing, a top Douyin influencer specializing in Peking Opera. Join host Yegor as we explore Peking Opera's history, immerse in its traditional artistic atmosphere, witness behind-the-scenes preparations and makeup processes, and discover the passion of today's youth for this art form. We'll also visit the Beijing Guoyi Children's Peking Opera Troupe to see how Peking Opera shapes the lives of young students.

programme.title: From Nubia to La Plata
programme.desc: In the early 1960s, Argentine Egyptologist Abraham Rosenvasser led an expedition to Sudan to excavate the Temple of Aksha. As the Nile rose, he rescued some of the temple's treasures and brought them to the La Plata Museum, where they are displayed today.

programme.title: The Journey of Rice Ep.1
programme.desc: By tracing how rice spread from China to dining tables around the word, reexamine the evolution of Chinese civilization and its global influence.

programme.title: Quanzhou Nanyin: A Living Fossil in the History of Chinese Music
programme.desc: Nanyin, also known as "Quanzhou Nanyin," is an ancient Han Chinese musical tradition whose singing style preserves the time-honored ethnic vocal techniques predating the Tang Dynasty, earning it the title of "a living fossil in the history of Chinese music." The program features Yegor, a Ukrainian music enthusiast, visiting Master Su Shuyong, a Nanyin inheritor, to hear her decades-long stories of teaching this art. They also tour the Quanzhou Nanyin Troupe, where, led by its artistic director Zhuang Lifen, they learn about the basic performance formats and instruments of Nanyin. Additionally, the episode follows a post-1990s Nanyin performer, Zheng Mingming, as she sips tea with guests at sunset, reflecting on the deep-rooted role Nanyin plays in the daily lives of Quanzhou's people.

programme.title: Guqin Music Art
programme.desc: The guqin is an instrument with a history of over 3,000 years. Yet in all that time, its design and sound have remained virtually unchanged. In 2003, the guqin and its music were proclaimed as part of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity by UNESCO. But how has this ancient instrument withstood the musical test of time? How do its slow, gentle melodies resonate in fast-paced modern China? In this episode of The Inheritors, we explore guqin music art's history, development in modern days, and its future.

programme.desc: It’s been 20 years in the making — the return of the drag racing reality TV show that started it all. New host Bruno Massel. New network. Built by automotive enthusiasts, for automotive enthusiasts. In Episode 1, we take you along for the full journey — from the origins of PINKS racing to today’s PINKS 2.0 competition at Rockingham Dragway. You’ll meet the racers who put it all on the line and step into the legendary PINKS Circle. The road wasn’t easy. Breakdowns, setbacks, and hurdles stood in the way, and every racer had to fight just to make it to the track and earn their shot to compete. Sit back and enjoy the ride as we bring you PINKS 2.0.
